Definition: a valve of a folding door (as turning); also a ring (as round)
BiblicalUsage: Galil means a folding leaf, a valve of a door that turns, and also a ring. The two doors of the temple were of fir tree, and the two leaves of the one door were folding, in 1 Kings 6:34. The same word is a ring: the hangings were fastened to silver rings in Esther 1:6, and the beloved's hands are as gold rings set with the beryl in Song of Solomon 5:14.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the folding door and the gold ring show how one word can hold two beauties. A door that turns and a ring that shines both belong to God's house, and I hold that He makes the useful beautiful and the beautiful useful.
